target_customer: African diaspora and migrants sending money home (consumers), and payment firms using its Rafiki payout infrastructure
problem: Sending money to and within East Africa was costly and often needed internet or bank access. NALA started with offline mobile money payments and moved to cross-border transfers.
business_model: remittance and FX fees plus B2B payout API (Rafiki)

founders.name: Benjamin Fernandes
previous_startups: 2011 mobile money service for paying TV subscriptions in East Africa
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch March 2021 says he was a national TV host and built the 2011 service; education not stated. Tech.eu 2024 names no other founders.

technical_complexity.rationale: Integrating many mobile money operators and later multi-currency ledgers and licensed money transmission is hard engineering plus compliance, though built on standard components.

defensibility.rationale: Licenses (US money transmitter via Nala Payments LLC per a profile) and payout network integrations take time, but remittance rivals are large and well funded.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: WorldRemit bought Sendwave in August 2020 for 500M USD (TechCrunch 2021); NALA stayed independent and launched Rafiki in 2024.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (March 2021) reports 250,000 users within a year of launch and that about one in seven users wanted to receive money from abroad.

branding.domain_note: Now uses nala.com; earlier branded as Nala Money (a profile said it was formerly Nala Money).

identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline: Making Money Move; The Global Account for The Next Billion

brand_strength.rationale: Claims 1 million users in 35 countries and Forbes Fintech 50 mention; name is shared with other brands and no brand specific press found.

pivots.from: Offline mobile money payments app in Tanzania
pivots.why: Users wanted to receive money from abroad (TechCrunch 2021); B2B launch reported in March 2024

outcome_analysis: NALA, the first East African company through YC per TechCrunch, started as an offline mobile money app, took a 2019 pre-seed from Accel, moved into remittances in 2020, raised a 10M seed in 2022 and a 40M Series A in 2024, and added the Rafiki B2B rails. It is active and independent with over 1 million users claimed.
notes: Competitors left empty: TechCrunch March 2021 names WorldRemit and Mama Money, nearly two years after the W19 batch, so not used. Pre-seed amount only described as seven figures (FF News and a search snippet); recorded with null amount. Series A total over 50M per Tech.eu. A StartupList item of a 25M debt financing in May 2026 is unverified and not recorded. CTO Nicolas Esteves is described as CTO but not as co-founder, so not listed. YC page says founded 2022 while sources say 2017 or 2018.
